correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and first tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies a narrow vegetated mountain drainage entering the west-to-east valley from the southwest. The headward image shows its northward bend and connection with the wider valley, followed by the next northern tributary junction. The selected opening itself does not cross an observable lake or glacier. The historical federal profile describes Torrecillas as the outlet of Laguna Malargüe and separately lists Colorado among its tributaries, but it does not locate the selected feeder well enough to assign either name to that first reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Mountain valley, eastward trunk and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The connected mountain valley turns northeast, then east through several visible tributary junctions before curving southeast toward the foothill outlet. This is the mountain corridor described by the federal profile as Torrecillas continuing as Malargüe, with northern Negro-Calabozo and Minas/Pincheira contributions. No separate selected tributary fragment or reservoir crossing is present. The documentary name changes are retained without inventing exact boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Foothill outlet, managed reach and Malargüe town approach
correspondence.finding: The valley opens onto the plain south of the settlement and cultivated blocks. Imagery continuously depicts the river corridor through the foothill outlet and irrigation-control setting to the road crossing. Before the Aquabook map failure, DGI prose identified Blas Brísoli as a diversion structure on Malargüe and Cañada Colorada as its off-taking irrigation canal. This supports a managed river reach, without assigning the selected line to the canal or claiming contemporary operation, reservoir storage, or exact structure coordinates.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern alluvial-plain excursion and return toward the receiving wetland
correspondence.finding: East of the road crossing, the selected route turns southeast away from the broad eastward river corridor, follows the northern edge of a separate agricultural block, continues east across the plain, and turns northeast toward the wetland drainage. The complete imagery covers this excursion, including field edges, minor traces and the more conspicuous river/wetland belt to its north. It does not establish the selected southern excursion and its return as one connected river or managed passage. Regional Malargüe-to-Llancanelo prose cannot supply that missing through-link. The issue is a distinct corridor choice, not exact bank alignment or lack of visible flowing water.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern receiving plain and wetland approach
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation traverses the broad saline/alluvial lowland and turns south through the western Llancanelo wetland setting. Imagery covers the interlaced channels, pale surfaces and lakeward wetland tongues throughout. This identifies the receiving setting but does not independently settle the selected branch sequence downstream of the unresolved agricultural excursion. No additional primary pending status is assigned for this same lower through-link problem.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake entry and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected continuation lies in the western lake/shore belt of Llancanelo and ends within that receiving basin. The terminal image shows wetland tongues entering the lake, water and exposed saline shoreline; the federal profile identifies Llancanelo as the Malargüe receiving lake. A separate river line across the lake surface is not required. The selected endorheic terminal class is retained as supplied metadata; no current lake level, present isolation, precise mouth, or active-flow claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and long southward inland-ice approach
correspondence.finding: The northern opening and long southward approach lie on the mapped Inland Ice west of the coastal bedrock belt. The southern end of this first part reaches the irregular ice and exposed-rock margin. The map distinguishes this whole approach from the adjoining colored bedrock units; its blue surface-contour and sub-ice thematic lines are not river channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward bend in the exposed-rock and ice-margin belt
correspondence.finding: All short parts of the upper westward bend are covered by the original map in the irregular exposed-rock/nunatak and adjoining ice-margin belt north of Waltershausen Gletscher. The selected line crosses generalized mapped bedrock units and their margins; the original supplies geographic correspondence, but does not depict this bend as one named river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward sequence and southern turn through the rock-margin indentation
correspondence.finding: The successive southwestward parts and their southern turn are visible across the same bedrock belt and its narrow intervening ice-filled indentation. Both the colored rock bodies and the adjoining glacier/ice ground are accounted for at ordinary regional scale, including the join into the next southeastward passage. No natural-river channel or name is inferred from the geological unit boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Connecting south/east passage into the Waltershausen glacier setting
correspondence.finding: The complete south/east connecting passage is covered through the narrow rock-and-ice-margin zone into the broader glacier setting bearing the Waltershausen Gletscher label. The part joins are geographically visible in the continuous original coverage. Waltershausen Gletscher identifies the mapped glacier context, not a river or a whole-object hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate southeastward glacier and bedrock-margin sequence
correspondence.finding: All successive southeastward parts are covered along the mapped glacier corridor and adjoining exposed-rock margin west of Hudson Land. The original distinguishes the pale glacier ground from the geological units on either side. The selected passage is geographically accounted for without asserting a surveyed river or a surface/subglacial hydraulic connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower glacier corridor and approach to the historical ice front
correspondence.finding: The complete lower southeastward sequence is visible in the narrowing Waltershausen Gletscher corridor between mapped bedrock flanks. Its approach to the historical glacier front and adjoining inner fjord setting is exposed in the enlarged original. No lake, reservoir or managed connector is established in this section.

correspondence.component_scope: Final selected part and actual displayed ending
correspondence.finding: The final selected part and its actual displayed endpoint are accounted for at the mapped historical glacier-front/inner-fjord transition at the southeastern end of Waltershausen Gletscher. The regional original also shows the adjoining fjord connection toward the labeled Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord. This establishes the ordinary terminal geographic setting, not an ordinary river mouth, an exact source-epoch ice-front intersection or a modern glacier-front position. The model sea-terminal class is not independent source proof.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen inland-ice opening and initial east/southeast passage
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and first east/southeast section lie within the original map’s inland-ice and near-nunatak setting in the Mont Forel region. All stored parts and intervening joins were compared in the same continuous source view. The blue and grey inland-ice linework is not read as river hydrography.

correspondence.component_scope: Easternmost bend and long southward passage
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern bend and ensuing southward passage are covered across the transition from inland ice to elongated exposed-rock bodies separated by ice. The source depicts the geographic terrain throughout this long component; it does not depict or name one continuous natural river on the modeled line.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern intermediate ice and exposed-rock corridor
correspondence.finding: The intermediate southwestern sequence and its many short stored joins lie in the mapped mixed ice/exposed-rock belt. The corridor between successive rock bodies and the next southward passage are visible without a geographic coverage break.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward connector and lower southward bend
correspondence.finding: The westward connector and the longer lower bend remain in mapped ice and exposed-rock terrain, including the narrow passage between adjacent rock bodies. Geographic correspondence is established for the whole stored sequence; blue contour or other thematic lines do not prove channel continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southwestern approach to the coastal margin
correspondence.finding: The lower southwestern sequence approaches the eastern inner Sermilik coastal-margin setting through the original’s historical ice/exposed-rock mosaic. Both intervening turns and the westward lower passage are covered. No named lake, reservoir, managed connector or natural-river reach is established for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Final stage-3 passage and inter-fragment join
correspondence.finding: The last stage-3 parts and the join to FID8884 occur in the mapped exposed-rock/ice coastal-margin belt immediately inland of the inner fjord setting. The joined fragments were read together with the actual ending rather than stopping at a nearby fjord label.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage-2 terminal fragment and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: The complete short terminal continuation and its final bend are covered in the same historical exposed-rock/ice coastal-margin setting at inner Sermilik. At this source scale, the endpoint is at the mapped land/ice margin beside the fjord head. The model’s sea-ending class is not independent evidence of a surveyed river mouth. No current glacier-front, exact waterline or natural-river mouth claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and upper named reaches
correspondence.finding: The selected opening corresponds to the small headward drainage entering the Las Flores/Pancochá corridor near the western Mixco/Santiago Sacatepéquez setting. The source follows that connected corridor east and southeast through the Pansalic junction into Río Molino beside Mixco, then south toward Villalobos. The short initial feeder has no separately established name. Río Pansalic is an entering tributary, not an alias of the selected upper corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Molino–Villalobos continuation and lake-entry setting
correspondence.finding: The original cartography continuously follows Molino past the separately joining San Lucas river, then labels Villalobos through Villa Nueva/Petapa toward Villa Canales and its lake-entry delta. The Frutal, Pinula and Platanitos joins remain distinct tributary context. Both upper sheets overlap on this corridor; the broad alluvial entry and continuing lake setting are visible in independent imagery.

correspondence.component_scope: Lago de Amatitlán passage and western outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the lake’s eastern/delta setting, traverses the connected lake basins through the El Relleno neck and continues northwest to the Amatitlán outlet. Original lake cartography and the bounded imagery view establish the waterbody passage, including its built crossing setting. The lake remains a separate named feature; its interior is not assigned the river name. The source depicts the river leaving the western outlet into the Michatoya valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Michatoya through Palín and Escuintla
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Amatitlán, Palín and Escuintla originals follow the southwest river valley through Palín and south beside Escuintla, then southeast across the lower alluvial corridor. The mapped Embalse Jurún Marinalá setting and continuing channel are included. The selected river corridor is not equated with a separate hydroelectric diversion or tunnel, and no operating-state claim is needed. Intervening tributary joins are included at ordinary map scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Michatoya joining the María Linda corridor
correspondence.finding: The southern source cartography labels Michatoya and the adjoining Astachillo/María Linda drainage separately. Where hazard colors obscure their meeting, the final bounded imagery view shows the western river corridor meeting the eastern receiving river and the resulting southward continuation. This establishes the selected through-link at ordinary corridor scale. Astachillo is retained as adjacent named drainage, not a wholesale alias or replacement name for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: María Linda lower floodplain and approach to Iztapa
correspondence.finding: Masagua and Iztapa originals depict and directly label the continuing María Linda river through the lower floodplain toward Iztapa. The source shows neighbouring lagunetas, minor drainage and estuarine widening; those adjacent waterbodies are not treated as selected lake passages. The selected bends and the approach to the fragment boundary remain in this connected lower river.

correspondence.component_scope: Final fragment and actual Iztapa coastal ending
correspondence.finding: The final fragment continues directly from FID10637 in the María Linda estuarine corridor at Iztapa/Puerto Viejo and ends at its coastal-bar/shore setting. The source map labels the river and Pacific coast. Independent imagery follows the river into the connected shore-parallel estuary and visible Pacific inlet. The rendered ending is assessed within that mouth complex; it is not silently relocated to the lateral present inlet or claimed to mark a surveyed active opening through the bar.
